```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(caret)
library(rpart)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(20261012)
```

## Overview

The objective is to predict the quality of a barbell lift using accelerometers worn on the belt, arm, forearm, and dumbbell. The target variable, `classe`, has five categories (A–E). The provided training dataset contains `r nrow(read.csv('pml-training.csv', nrows=20000))` observations. Twenty separately supplied test cases are reserved for course grading and are not used to assess performance.

## Reading the data and partitioning

```{r load-data}
training_raw <- read.csv('pml-training.csv', na.strings = c('NA', '#DIV/0!', ''), check.names = TRUE)
testing_raw <- read.csv('pml-testing.csv', na.strings = c('NA', '#DIV/0!', ''), check.names = TRUE)
training_raw$classe <- factor(training_raw$classe)
stopifnot(nrow(testing_raw) == 20)
set.seed(20261012)
idx <- createDataPartition(training_raw$classe, p = 0.75, list = FALSE)
train_raw <- training_raw[idx, , drop = FALSE]
valid_raw <- training_raw[-idx, , drop = FALSE]
table(train_raw$classe)
```

Predictors are chosen using **only the training partition**. We discard metadata that could leak activity/session identity, predictors with 5% or more missing entries, nonnumeric columns, and near-zero-variance predictors. The remaining variables describe physical sensor measurements. We apply the same columns to validation and course-testing data.

```{r feature-cleaning}
metadata <- c('X', 'user_name', 'raw_timestamp_part_1',
              'raw_timestamp_part_2', 'cvtd_timestamp',
              'new_window', 'num_window', 'problem_id')
features <- setdiff(intersect(names(train_raw), names(testing_raw)),
                    c(metadata, 'classe'))
features <- features[vapply(train_raw[features], is.numeric, logical(1))]
features <- features[colMeans(is.na(train_raw[features])) < 0.05]
nzv <- nearZeroVar(train_raw[features])
if (length(nzv)) features <- features[-nzv]
features <- features[vapply(train_raw[features], function(x) all(is.finite(x)), logical(1)) &
                     vapply(valid_raw[features], function(x) all(is.finite(x)), logical(1)) &
                     vapply(testing_raw[features], function(x) all(is.finite(x)), logical(1))]
stopifnot(length(features) > 0)
train <- data.frame(train_raw[features], classe = train_raw$classe)
valid <- data.frame(valid_raw[features], classe = valid_raw$classe)
cat('Number of predictors:', length(features), '\n')
cat('Training observations:', nrow(train), '\n')
cat('Holdout observations:', nrow(valid), '\n')
```

## Model and cross-validation

A single CART tree is an interpretable baseline. The primary model is **bagged classification trees**, built through `caret` using the `ipred` package already available in the lab. Bagging reduces the variance of individual trees and can capture nonlinear relationships and interactions without scaling features. We use stratified 75%/25% training/holdout partitions, and **three-fold cross-validation within the training partition**. The holdout is assessed only after training.

```{r model-fit, cache=TRUE}
ctrl <- trainControl(method = 'cv', number = 3)
set.seed(20261012)
cart <- train(classe ~ ., data = train, method = 'rpart',
              trControl = ctrl, metric = 'Accuracy',
              tuneGrid = data.frame(cp = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05)))
set.seed(20261012)
bagged <- train(classe ~ ., data = train, method = 'treebag',
                trControl = ctrl, metric = 'Accuracy')
print(cart)
print(bagged)
```

## Out-of-sample evaluation

```{r evaluation}
cart_pred <- predict(cart, newdata = valid)
bagged_pred <- predict(bagged, newdata = valid)
cart_cm <- confusionMatrix(cart_pred, valid$classe)
bagged_cm <- confusionMatrix(bagged_pred, valid$classe)
cart_accuracy <- as.numeric(cart_cm$overall['Accuracy'])
bagged_accuracy <- as.numeric(bagged_cm$overall['Accuracy'])
score_table <- data.frame(Model = c('Single CART tree', 'Bagged trees'),
                          Holdout_Accuracy = round(c(cart_accuracy, bagged_accuracy), 4),
                          Holdout_Error = round(1 - c(cart_accuracy, bagged_accuracy), 4))
knitr::kable(score_table)
print(bagged_cm$table)
```

The bagged model attained **`r sprintf('%.2f%%', 100 * bagged_accuracy)` holdout accuracy**, equivalent to an observed holdout misclassification rate of **`r sprintf('%.2f%%', 100 * (1 - bagged_accuracy))`**. The holdout estimate gives a reasonable indication of expected out-of-sample error for observations drawn from a comparable distribution. It is not a guarantee for new participants or new recording sessions, which could introduce distribution shifts. The single-tree baseline attained `r sprintf('%.2f%%', 100 * cart_accuracy)` holdout accuracy. Cross-validation was used for model training and selection, not as a substitute for untouched holdout evaluation.

## Final model and twenty test predictions

After evaluating the approach, we refit the bagged model to all **19,622 labeled examples**, using exactly the selected sensor columns, and predict the 20 unlabeled cases. These predictions are not evaluated using the holdout set or quiz answers.

```{r final-predictions, cache=TRUE}
full_train <- data.frame(training_raw[features], classe = training_raw$classe)
course_test <- testing_raw[features]
stopifnot(all(vapply(full_train[features], function(x) all(is.finite(x)), logical(1))))
stopifnot(all(vapply(course_test, function(x) all(is.finite(x)), logical(1))))
set.seed(20261012)
final_model <- train(classe ~ ., data = full_train, method = 'treebag',
                     trControl = trainControl(method = 'none'))
predictions <- as.character(predict(final_model, newdata = course_test))
stopifnot(length(predictions) == 20)
prediction_table <- data.frame(problem_id = testing_raw$problem_id,
                               prediction = predictions)
knitr::kable(prediction_table)
write.csv(prediction_table, 'pml_predictions.csv', row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(predictions, 'pml_predictions.txt')
```

## Conclusions

Wearable sensor measurements provide useful signals for discriminating among the five lifting-quality categories. Filtering metadata and mostly missing columns reduces accidental leakage and limits the model to sensor features. Bagged trees learn nonlinear relationships without making a linearity assumption. Internal cross-validation and a separate 25% holdout provide distinct checks on performance; the reported expected error is the held-out misclassification rate. The submitted 20 predictions are generated by the final model trained on all available labeled observations.
